def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    cities = d["cities"]
    demand = d["demand"]
    arc = d["arc"]

    model.Cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)
    model.Arcs = pyo.Set(initialize=list(arc.keys()), dimen=2)

    # x[i,j] = units shipped from city i to city j
    def x_bounds(m, i, j):
        return (0, arc[(i, j)][1])

    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.Arcs, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=x_bounds
    )

    # Objective: minimize total transportation cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(arc[(i, j)][0] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in arc)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Flow balance per city: inflow - outflow = demand[i]
    # (demand positive = net demand, negative = net supply)
    def balance_rule(m, k):
        inflow = sum(m.x[i, k] for (i, j) in arc if j == k)
        outflow = sum(m.x[k, j] for (i, j) in arc if i == k)
        return inflow - outflow == demand[k]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.Cities, rule=balance_rule)

    # Capacity limits (also enforced via variable bounds; explicit here)
    def cap_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] <= arc[(i, j)][1]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.Arcs, rule=cap_rule)

    return model
